## Why the two fits differ — the premise needs one correction first

I reproduced every fit. The surprising finding: **on the archived 109-sample JSON, the algebraic and geometric objectives do not disagree**. Pure Kasa gives (−3767, +1476, −3985) / 44.30 µT; Kasa+LM gives (−3783, +1521, −3912) / 44.01 µT — a gap of only 16/45/73 counts. The (−4169, +1447, −5135) / 47.5 µT values are the 2026-09-15 documented fit, whose original capture (`photos/mag_tilt.json`) was never archived; **no consistent fit of the archived file reproduces them**, so the two numbers are not "two objectives on the same data." The concrete mechanisms, each verified:

- **Objective function / numerics** — The algebraic (Kasa) normal equations are ill-conditioned on this data: samples sit 4000–9000 counts from the origin, matrix entries span 10²–10⁹, cond ≈ 1.3×10⁸ (2×10⁷ even after centring). Two mathematically equivalent Kasa formulations scatter by 400–560 counts centroided and >2000 counts uncentred — and one variant lands at x = −4164, within 5 counts of the documented −4169. So a naive algebraic solve can plausibly emit the documented values; the LM geometric fit (unit-cosine Jacobian) converges to the same point from any start, including from the documented centre. The algebraic result on this data is implementation-dependent; the geometric one is not.
- **Partial-arc coverage** — Octant populations range 3–32 samples (mean resultant length 0.23), and axis half-spans (6803/7144/7714 counts) show ±7–13% soft-iron anisotropy. The centre is weakly constrained along z and slides by hundreds of counts under perturbation.
- **Noise / environment** — RMS is 4.63 µT = 10.5% of radius, which **fails the project's own ≤8% gate** (`fit_mag_sphere.py` exits 1). The capture is pre-fix, taken near the workbench with the measured 184 µT anomaly — exactly the situation the 8% gate was created to reject.

## Which centre is trustworthy, and what to bake

**Keep the firmware values: (−4169, +1447, −5135) with scales (1.000/1.069/0.939).** The hardware validation is closed-loop physical evidence and outweighs any offline fit statistic: with these values baked in, Fusion's magnetic error fell 90° → 0–1°, stationary yaw stopped drifting, |B| became orientation-invariant (35–56 µT, stationary σ = 0.17 µT vs σ = 20 before), and the fitted radius 47.5 µT equals the local IGRF total field at 31°N. The refit of the archived JSON fails the project's own acceptance gate, so by the project's own criteria it is a rejected fit, not a candidate. Do not "update" the firmware to (−3783, +1521, −3912).

## Recommendation (one paragraph)

The discrepancy is not Kasa-versus-LM — on identical data those agree within ~0.5 µT — but an unstable algebraic solve on partial-coverage, contaminated data, compared against a hardware-validated value whose original capture was never archived. Trust the firmware centre, because its evidence is the device itself behaving correctly (em 0–1°, orientation-invariant |B|, radius matching the local geomagnetic field), while the archived-data refit fails the project's own 8% RMS rejection gate. Bake nothing new; instead treat this as a reproducibility lesson: if recalibration is ever redone, capture a fresh tumble ≥1 m from the desk, fit with the geometric (LM) objective (Kasa only as a centroided initializer), require both gates (RMS ≤ 8%, radius 25–65 µT), confirm on-device via `em` and |B| invariance, and archive the raw capture alongside the values it produced.
